correctness.rationale: Greedy left/right subsequence occurrence lemma is proved for each position. Compositionality and the adjacent-repeat/factor-extension lemmas justify the complete 147-element primitive-candidate universe (counts 3,6,12,18,30,36,30,12,0). A deterministic exhaustive test of all 3^n words at each 1<=n<=11 then shows no shorter ambiguity and exactly six length-eleven words, each with precisely two length-six covers. A separate positional-embedding algorithm agrees on 127530 small inputs and certifies every witness plus all shorter-cover exclusions; actual code and output are embedded.

value.rationale: The first possible nonuniqueness length of shortest subsequence covers over a fixed minimal nonbinary alphabet is a natural sharp extremal boundary. The theorem strengthens an earlier existence example using four symbols and length fifteen by proving a ternary length-eleven witness is minimum and classifying all six labeled minimal witnesses. It resolves a focused finite structural question about a nonstandard covering notion, supported by complete finite exhaustion rather than an arbitrary small tabulation.
